Chapter 6: The Call of the Old Country—Returning to the Source
Have you ever felt that tug—the one that starts deep inside you, pulling you back toward your roots? There comes a point when the stories you’ve heard and the memories you’ve carried just aren’t enough anymore. Suddenly, the urge to see the land your ancestors called home is so strong, you can’t ignore it.
So, the decision’s made. It’s not easy—there’s excitement, sure, but also this quiet fear. What if you don’t fit in? What if you’re seen as a stranger in the very place that shaped your family’s history?
Picture yourself stepping onto a plane, carrying more than just your suitcase. You’re carrying generations of hopes, dreams, and unanswered questions. When you finally land in Armenia, the view out the window feels both familiar and completely new. The language you used to hear at home suddenly surrounds you. Faces in the crowd echo the features of people you’ve only seen in faded photos. The rhythm of life here? It sounds a lot like the stories your parents and grandparents used to tell.
Meeting distant relatives is a mix of comfort and awkwardness. There are hugs that linger, tears that surprise you, and laughter that fills the room. And yet, there are also those moments when words just aren’t enough—when you realize that, while you share blood, years apart have shaped you differently. But even then, there’s this undeniable sense of coming home. You feel like some part of you has been waiting for this all along.
As you wander through old streets, step into churches, and browse bustling markets, you can’t help but notice the resilience in the people around you. The scars of history are visible—monuments that speak of loss, memories that refuse to fade. And yet, life carries on. Kids play in the alleys, elders gather to swap stories, and the everyday rhythm never misses a beat. It hits you that the past isn’t just something heavy to carry—it’s also a source of strength.
Then, there’s that afternoon when you finally see the village where your parents were born. The old house is gone, replaced by something new, but the land—the land is the same. Standing there, you feel a connection that words can’t really express. It’s a sense of belonging that’s both incredibly deep and somehow just out of reach. For a moment, everything feels clear. You realize your identity isn’t just rooted in memories—it’s tied to this place, too.
Heading back, you know this isn’t the end of your story. It’s a fresh beginning. You leave with a heart that’s a little quieter, but a whole lot fuller. The pain and beauty of your heritage are woven together now, and the stories you’ve carried have taken on new meaning. You’re ready to carry them forward—to let them shape the next chapter of your journey.
